report.source_text: an MRI of the brain was performed, which revealed a saccular basilar artery aneurysm measuring 4.7 cm in the largest diameter, located in the mid part of the basilar artery. The aneurysm demonstrated a characteristic saccular morphology with an intact, yet irregular, wall. Within the aneurysm, a non-occlusive thrombus was identified. There was evidence of a significant pressure effect on the brainstem, manifesting as marked narrowing of the pons and medulla oblongata. Surrounding vascular anatomy appeared patent with normal caliber. The aneurysmal wall did not show any signs of rupture (Figure 1).

report.source_text: During her hospital stay, the patient experienced a gradual resolution of her headaches. This positive response was accompanied by stability in neurological examinations. The absence of new neurological deficits and the alleviation of symptoms were promising signs of the success of the endovascular coiling procedure.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old female with well-controlled hypertension presented to the neurology clinic with a 3-month history of persistent, severe headaches accompanied by nausea and photophobia. Initial vital signs were normal, and neurological examination revealed no focal deficits, cognitive impairment, or meningeal signs; fundoscopic evaluation showed no papilledema. MRI brain on admission revealed a large 4.7 cm saccular basilar artery aneurysm located in the mid basilar artery with characteristic saccular morphology, an intact but irregular wall, and a non-occlusive intramural thrombus. The aneurysm exerted significant mass effect on the brainstem, causing marked narrowing of the pons and medulla oblongata, with no evidence of rupture. Routine laboratory investigations (complete blood count and basic metabolic panel) were normal. The patient underwent endovascular intervention under general anesthesia involving placement of a flow-diverter stent and precise deployment of coils within the aneurysm, with a procedure duration of approximately 2 hours. During the hospital stay, the patient experienced gradual resolution of her headaches with stability on neurological examinations and no new neurological deficits, indicating successful treatment response.
